introduction-the-elasticity-engine.core: An Auto Scaling group maintains a fleet of EC2 instances between min and max sizes: it replaces unhealthy instances, balances across AZs and scales with policies (target tracking, step, scheduled, predictive). It's the core elasticity primitive behind EC2-based services, ECS capacity and EKS managed node groups.

first_principles.problem: A fleet sized for peak wastes money at night and still falls over during unexpected spikes.

analogy.title: A thermostat for compute
analogy.story: Set the target and it adds or removes heat to stay there.
analogy.breaks: Heaters warm up instantly; instances take minutes to boot.

code.text:
aws autoscaling put-scaling-policy --auto-scaling-group-name web --policy-name cpu50 \
  --policy-type TargetTrackingScaling \
  --target-tracking-configuration '{"PredefinedMetricSpecification":{"PredefinedMetricType":"ASGAverageCPUUtilization"},"TargetValue":50}'

check.q: Why use ELB health checks on an ASG?
check.a: They replace instances that are running but failing application health checks, not just EC2 status checks.

launch-templates-vs-launch-configuration.core: Launch templates are versioned specifications for instances (AMI, instance type, IAM profile, security groups, user data, block devices, metadata options) and support mixed instance types, Spot, and newer features. Launch configurations are legacy, immutable and unsupported for new instance types and features, so use launch templates.

first_principles.problem: A team still on launch configurations can't use mixed instances, IMDSv2 enforcement or new instance types.
truths: Fleets benefit from multiple instance types.

analogy.title: A versioned recipe book versus a laminated card
analogy.story: You can publish improved recipes as new versions; the card can't change.
analogy.breaks: Recipes don't break if old; launch configurations block new instance types and features.

check.a: They're legacy, immutable and don't support new instance types, mixed instances or newer features.

lifecycle-hooks-the-pause-button.core: Lifecycle hooks pause instances in Pending:Wait (launch) or Terminating:Wait (termination) so you can run custom actions: install software, register with systems, warm caches, drain connections or upload logs. A heartbeat timeout bounds the pause, and CompleteLifecycleAction continues or abandons.

first_principles.problem: Scale-in kills instances mid-job and loses their logs; new instances serve traffic before they're ready.

analogy.title: A pit stop before entering and leaving the race
analogy.story: Cars are checked before joining, and safely parked before leaving.
analogy.breaks: Pit stops are seconds; hooks can wait up to 2 hours (extendable with heartbeats).

example.title: Graceful termination
flow: SSM Run Command: stop worker, flush logs to S3

check.q: What happens if no CompleteLifecycleAction is sent before the timeout?
check.a: The ASG applies the hook's default result (CONTINUE or ABANDON).

warm-pools-cheating-the-boot-time.core: Warm pools keep pre-initialised instances (stopped, hibernated or running) alongside an ASG. On scale-out, the ASG moves warm instances into service in seconds instead of launching and bootstrapping from scratch. Stopped instances cost only EBS storage, making fast scaling affordable for slow-booting apps.

first_principles.problem: An app takes 8 minutes to boot and warm up, so autoscaling lags behind traffic spikes.
truths: Boot and init dominate scale-out time.
derivation: Create a **warm pool** (min size, max prepared).
Use **lifecycle hooks** to finish init before entering warm state.

analogy.title: Pre-heated ovens on standby
analogy.story: When a rush comes, you just switch them on instead of waiting for them to heat up.
analogy.breaks: Ovens lose heat; stopped instances lose in-memory state unless hibernated.

code.text:
aws autoscaling put-warm-pool --auto-scaling-group-name web \
  --pool-state Stopped --min-size 4 --instance-reuse-policy ReuseOnScaleIn=true

check.q: What do you pay for instances in a Stopped warm pool?
check.a: Mainly their EBS volumes (and any Elastic IPs), not compute.

putting-it-all-together-the-production-p.core: A production ASG combines a versioned launch template (golden AMI, IMDSv2), a mixed instances policy (On-Demand base + diversified Spot), multi-AZ subnets, ELB health checks, target tracking plus predictive scaling, lifecycle hooks for bootstrap and drain, warm pools for fast scale-out, and instance refresh with checkpoints for rolling AMI updates.

first_principles.problem: Teams use ASGs with defaults and get slow scaling, ungraceful terminations and risky AMI rollouts.
truths: Each feature solves a specific problem.
derivation: **Instance refresh** with min healthy % and checkpoints.

analogy.title: A well-run airline fleet
analogy.story: Standard aircraft specs, mixed leasing, pre-flight checks, standby planes and scheduled maintenance rotations.
analogy.breaks: Aircraft are rotated over months; instance refresh can roll a fleet in an hour.

check.a: Replaces instances in an ASG gradually (respecting minimum healthy percentage and checkpoints) to roll out a new launch template or AMI.
